text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.66% today, extending a strong two-week rally of over 22%. The immediate driver was escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—container ships attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Aramco facilities hit, and Iran threatening U.S. warships—which pushed crude oil prices up sharply (Brent crude hit $125/barrel). Refining margins tend to widen when crude climbs while gasoline and diesel prices lag, and that setup favors refiners like Marathon; the company is also positioned to benefit from the diesel supply crunch the IEA warned is likely to persist into 2027.

The broader context is that U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity right now, and diesel inventories are already lean at 105 million barrels. When geopolitical risk tightens crude supplies while refineries are already running hard, refiner profits can spike—which is exactly the environment the market is pricing in for Marathon over the past two weeks.
